# Plugins reference

<!-- generated by `pybiscus plugins doc`: edit the plugins' docstrings and field descriptions, not this file -->

Every plugin Pybiscus loads from the bundled manifests (`pybiscus-plugins/plugins-conf.yml` and
`pybiscus-plugins-hierarchical/plugins-conf.yml`), family by family: the `name:` a configuration gives it,
where it comes from, what it does, its configuration fields, and the shipped configurations of `configs/`
that use it. How to write one: [Plugins](plugins.md), [How-to](how-to.md). The privacy evaluation of
PR #44 (`pybiscus-plugins-privacy-evaluation/`, not finalized) is not described here: see
[privacy-evaluation.md](privacy-evaluation.md).

- [Data](#data): `cifar`, `randomvector`, `turbofan`, `mnist`, `vector_`, `hdfs`
- [Models](#models): `cifar`, `mnist_cnn`, `linearregression`, `lstm`, `noop`, `deeplog`, `onnxmodel`
- [Strategies](#strategies): `fedavg`, `fedavgm`, `fedprox`, `fedadam`, `fedyogi`, `fedadagrad`, `fedmedian`, `fedtrimmedavg`, `krum`, `bulyan`, `qfedavg`, `faulttolerantfedavg`, `fedavgwithaggregator`
- [Strategy decorators](#strategy-decorators): `metricdiffcompute`, `timediffcompute`, `visualizemodellayers`, `saveserverfitparams`, `saveclientsfitin`, `saveclientsfitres`, `personalizeclientsfitin`, `serverdpfixed`, `serverdpadaptive`, `clipping`, `fltrust`, `foolsgold`, `evaluateonly`, `upperlevellink`
- [Clients](#clients): `relay`
- [Loggers](#loggers): `rich`, `webhook`
- [Metrics loggers](#metrics-loggers): `tensorboard`, `webhook`, `wandb`
- [Result modifiers](#result-modifiers): `resultidentity`, `result * factor`, `client watermarking`
- [Stopping criteria](#stopping-criteria): `threshold`, `patience`, `maxduration`
- [Fit results aggregators](#fit-results-aggregators): `average`, `weightedaverage`

## Data

A dataset and how it is split into train, validation and test sections (`data:` of the server and of the clients).

### `cifar` — Cifar 10

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/data/cifar10`*

CIFAR-10 from torchvision: 32 x 32 colour images of 10 classes, 50,000 to train and 10,000 to test, read from the dataset's directories; the shared train, val, test, privacy and trusted sections choose the examples, the partition between clients and the loaders.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `train` | section | (section) | the training set: directory, loader options, indices file or partition between clients |
| `train.dir` | str | `'${root_dir}/datasets/train/'` | directory of the official train split |
| `train.batch_size` | int | `32` | examples per batch |
| `train.shuffle` | bool | `True` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `train.drop_last` | bool | `True` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `train.seed` | int (optional) | `None` | order of the shuffled batches, reproducible; random if unset |
| `train.indices` | str (optional) | `None` | file of the indices of the examples to train on (whitespace-separated); exclusive with partition |
| `train.partition` | section, see [configuration.md](configuration.md#data) | `None` | this client's share of the training examples, disjoint from the other clients' |
| `train.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | at most this many examples, the same on every run; all if unset |
| `val` | section | (section) | the validation set: source (official test split, holdout, indices file), loader options |
| `val.source` | 'official' \| 'holdout' \| 'indices' | `'official'` | where the validation examples come from |
| `val.dir` | str | `'${root_dir}/datasets/val/'` | directory of the official test split (source: official) |
| `val.fraction` | float | `0.1` | share of the client's training examples held out (source: holdout) |
| `val.seed` | int | `42` | draw of the held-out examples (source: holdout) |
| `val.indices` | str (optional) | `None` | file of the indices of the validation examples (source: indices) |
| `val.batch_size` | int | `32` | examples per batch |
| `val.shuffle` | bool | `False` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `val.drop_last` | bool | `False` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `val.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | at most this many examples, the same on every run; all if unset |
| `test` | section | (section) | the testing set (required for the server): directory, loader options |
| `test.dir` | str | `'${root_dir}/datasets/test/'` | directory of the official test split |
| `test.batch_size` | int | `32` | examples per batch |
| `test.shuffle` | bool | `False` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `test.drop_last` | bool | `False` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `test.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | at most this many examples, the same on every run; all if unset |
| `privacy` | section | `None` | optional, the examples a server-side privacy evaluation attacks (the train split) |
| `privacy.dir` | str | `'${root_dir}/datasets/train/'` | directory of the official train split, whose examples are attacked |
| `privacy.batch_size` | int | `32` | examples per batch |
| `privacy.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | a fixed subset of at most this many examples, whose original indices stay known; all if unset |
| `trusted` | section | `None` | optional, the examples the server trains on to judge the clients' updates (fltrust) |
| `trusted.dir` | str | `'${root_dir}/datasets/train/'` | directory of the official train split, from which the trusted examples are drawn |
| `trusted.max_samples` | int | `500` | number of trusted examples, drawn at random from the train split |
| `trusted.seed` | int | `0` | draw of the trusted examples and order of their batches, reproducible |
| `trusted.batch_size` | int | `32` | examples per batch |
| `trusted.shuffle` | bool | `True` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `trusted.drop_last` | bool | `False` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `num_workers` | int | `0` | the number of workers for the DataLoaders (default to 0) |

### `turbofan` — Turbofan

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/data/turbofan`*

NASA C-MAPSS turbofan engines (the plugin's turbofan.txt holds engines 52, 62, 2, 64, 69). file: the engines' cycles (CSV); window: cycles fed to the model, never across two engines; normalize: each feature standardized with the statistics of all the train section's engines, before partition, so that every client computes the same ones (the server's train.engines must be the clients'); rul_clip: cap on the remaining useful life to predict (unset: none)

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | str | `'/home/elmo/Pybiscus/fromGithub/pybiscus/pybiscus-plugins/data/turbofan/turbofan.txt'` | the engines' cycles (CSV) |
| `window` | int | `20` | cycles fed to the model, never across two engines |
| `normalize` | bool | `True` | each feature standardized with the statistics of the train section's engines |
| `rul_clip` | int (optional) | `None` | cap on the remaining useful life to predict; none if unset |
| `train` | section | (section) | the engines the client trains on |
| `train.engines` | list[int] | (computed) | the engines whose cycles train the model; also set the normalization statistics |
| `train.batch_size` | int | `8` | examples per batch |
| `train.shuffle` | bool | `True` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `train.drop_last` | bool | `False` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `train.seed` | int (optional) | `None` | order of the shuffled batches, reproducible; random if unset |
| `train.partition` | section, see [configuration.md](configuration.md#data) | `None` | this client's share of the training examples, disjoint from the other clients' |
| `train.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | at most this many examples, the same on every run; all if unset |
| `val` | section | (section) | the engines the client validates on |
| `val.engines` | list[int] | (computed) | the engines whose cycles validate the model |
| `val.batch_size` | int | `8` | examples per batch |
| `val.shuffle` | bool | `False` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `val.drop_last` | bool | `False` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `val.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | at most this many examples, the same on every run; all if unset |
| `test` | section | (section) | the engines of the final evaluation (the server's) |
| `test.engines` | list[int] | (computed) | the engines whose cycles validate the model |
| `test.batch_size` | int | `8` | examples per batch |
| `test.shuffle` | bool | `False` | examples drawn in a new random order at every epoch |
| `test.drop_last` | bool | `False` | leave out the last, incomplete batch of every epoch |
| `test.max_samples` | int (optional) | `None` | at most this many examples, the same on every run; all if unset |
| `num_workers` | int | `0` | processes loading the batches; 0: the main process |

## Models

The model trained by the clients and evaluated by the server (`model:`); the server and the clients must name the same one.

### `cifar` — Cifar 10

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/model/cnn`*

A small convolutional network for the 32 x 32 colour images of CIFAR-10 (data `cifar`): reports its loss and accuracy.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `input_shape` | int | `3` | number of channels of the input |
| `mid_shape` | int | `6` | number of channels of the second convolutional layer |
| `n_classes` | int | `10` | number of classes |

### `onnxmodel` — ONNX model (evaluation only)

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/model/onnxmodel`*

Evaluates an ONNX graph on the site's data: no torch parameter, nothing to train or aggregate. The graph includes its preprocessing; the batch's inputs are given to it as they come from the data plugin.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | str | required | the .onnx file, deposited by each site |
| `sha256` | str | required | SHA-256 of the file, given by the session's organiser: another file is refused |
| `output_kind` | 'logits' \| 'probabilities' \| 'labels' \| 'regression' | `'logits'` | what the graph outputs: logits, probabilities, labels (class indices) or regression values |
| `input_name` | str (optional) | `None` | the graph's input to feed, its only input by default |
| `output_name` | str (optional) | `None` | the graph's output to read, its first output by default |
| `providers` | list[str] | `['CPUExecutionProvider']` | onnxruntime execution providers, by order of preference |
| `max_size_mb` | int | `2048` | a larger file is refused before being read (a single ONNX file stops at 2 GB) |
| `num_classes` | int (optional) | `None` | the number of classes, needed by class_rates |
| `class_rates` | 'none' \| 'per_class' \| 'confusion_matrix' | `'none'` | per-class figures for an exact F1; per_class and confusion_matrix tell the site's share of each class |

Used by: [`configs/onnx_eval/client_1.yml`](../configs/onnx_eval/client_1.yml), [`configs/onnx_eval/client_2.yml`](../configs/onnx_eval/client_2.yml), [`configs/onnx_eval/server.yml`](../configs/onnx_eval/server.yml)

## Strategies

How the server aggregates the clients' updates (`server_strategy.strategy`).

### `fedavg` — FedAvg

*core, `pybiscus/flower/strategy/fedavg`*

Parameters of Flower's FedAvg, see flwr.server.strategy.FedAvg.

| `fraction_evaluate` | float | `1` | fraction of the available clients that evaluate in each round |
| `min_fit_clients` | int | `2` | fewest clients that train in a round (set by the manager in a session) |
| `min_evaluate_clients` | int | `2` | fewest clients that evaluate in a round (set by the manager in a session) |
| `min_available_clients` | int | `2` | a round waits until this many clients are connected (set by the manager in a session) |
| `accept_failures` | bool | `True` | aggregate the round although some clients failed; refuse it otherwise |

| `accept_failures` | bool | `True` | aggregate the round although some clients failed; refuse it otherwise |

### `fedadam` — FedAdam

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategy/flowergeneric`*

Server-side Adam, see flwr.server.strategy.FedAdam. eta: server learning rate; tau: adaptivity (a tiny tau makes every step the sign of the update); eta_l: informative only (unused by Flower).

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fraction_fit` | float | `1` | fraction of the available clients that train in each round |
| `fraction_evaluate` | float | `1` | fraction of the available clients that evaluate in each round |

| `min_evaluate_clients` | int | `2` | fewest clients that evaluate in a round (set by the manager in a session) |
| `min_available_clients` | int | `2` | a round waits until this many clients are connected (set by the manager in a session) |
| `accept_failures` | bool | `True` | aggregate the round although some clients failed; refuse it otherwise |
| `eta` | float | `0.01` | server learning rate: the size of the step the server takes along the aggregated update |
| `eta_l` | float | `0.1` | the clients' learning rate, informative only: Flower does not use it |
| `beta_1` | float | `0.9` | decay of the first moment (momentum) of the server's Adam |
| `beta_2` | float | `0.99` | decay of the second moment of the server's Adam |
| `tau` | float | `1e-09` | adaptivity: added to the denominator; tiny, every step is about the sign of the update |

### `qfedavg` — QFedAvg

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategy/flowergeneric`*

q-Fair FedAvg, see flwr.server.strategy.QFedAvg. qffl_learning_rate: QFedAvg rebuilds each client's gradient as (w - w_client) / qffl_learning_rate, which assumes plain SGD steps at that rate; with momentum and many local steps, the clients' own rate (0.001 for cifar10) learned worst: 0.1 did best (launch/campaign, DEVLOG). Note: Flower weighs every client with the same loss, the global model's one evaluated by the server, so q does not favour the clients the global model serves badly.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fraction_fit` | float | `1` | fraction of the available clients that train in each round |
| `fraction_evaluate` | float | `1` | fraction of the available clients that evaluate in each round |
| `min_fit_clients` | int | `2` | fewest clients that train in a round (set by the manager in a session) |
| `min_evaluate_clients` | int | `2` | fewest clients that evaluate in a round (set by the manager in a session) |
| `min_available_clients` | int | `2` | a round waits until this many clients are connected (set by the manager in a session) |
| `accept_failures` | bool | `True` | aggregate the round although some clients failed; refuse it otherwise |
| `q_param` | float | `0.2` | fairness: the larger, the more weight to the clients with a high loss; 0: FedAvg-like |
| `qffl_learning_rate` | float | `0.1` | rate used to rebuild each client's gradient from its update (0.1 did best on cifar10) |

No configuration (`config: {empty_configuration: true}`).

### `serverdpfixed` — ServerDPFixedClipping

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategydecorator/serverdp`*

Central differential privacy with a fixed clipping norm, see flwr.server.strategy.DifferentialPrivacyServerSideFixedClipping. clipping_norm: bound C on the norm of each client's update (w_client - w_global); the clients' weight_drift under FedProx mu 0 shows its usual size.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `noise_multiplier` | float | `0.1` | z: the noise added to the aggregate has a standard deviation of z x C / num_sampled_clients |
| `num_sampled_clients` | int (optional) | `None` | clients per round in the noise's calibration; the strategy's min_fit_clients if unset |
| `delta` | float | `1e-05` | the epsilon reported is for this delta, when every client takes part in every round |
| `clipping_norm` | float | `1.0` | bound C on the norm of each client's update |

### `serverdpadaptive` — ServerDPAdaptiveClipping

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategydecorator/serverdp`*

Central differential privacy with a clipping norm adapted every round so that about target_clipped_quantile of the clients get clipped, see flwr.server.strategy.DifferentialPrivacyServerSideAdaptiveClipping (norm update corrected: CorrectedAdaptiveClipping). The count of clipped clients is noised too (clipped_count_stddev, num_sampled_clients / 20 if unset): Flower requires noise_multiplier < 2 * clipped_count_stddev.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `noise_multiplier` | float | `0.1` | z: the noise added to the aggregate has a standard deviation of z x C / num_sampled_clients |
| `num_sampled_clients` | int (optional) | `None` | clients per round in the noise's calibration; the strategy's min_fit_clients if unset |
| `delta` | float | `1e-05` | the epsilon reported is for this delta, when every client takes part in every round |
| `initial_clipping_norm` | float | `0.1` | bound C on the update norms in the first round, then adapted |
| `target_clipped_quantile` | float | `0.5` | fraction of the clients whose update the adapted C should clip |
| `clip_norm_lr` | float | `0.2` | how fast C moves towards the target quantile |
| `clipped_count_stddev` | float (optional) | `None` | noise on the count of clipped clients; num_sampled_clients / 20 if unset |

### `clipping` — Update norm clipping

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategydecorator/clipping`*

Robust aggregation: clips the clients' updates to a norm (fixed, or a multiple of their median) before the strategy aggregates them, and can reject the largest ones; see robust-aggregation.md.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | 'fixed' \| 'median' | `'median'` | fixed: updates clipped to clipping_norm; median: to median_factor x the round's median update norm, set by itself, without lag, and which a minority of clients cannot move |
| `median_factor` | float | `1.5` | mode median: updates are clipped to this many times the round's median update norm |
| `clipping_norm` | float | `2.0` | mode fixed: updates are clipped to this norm |
| `reject_factor` | float (optional) | `None` | clients whose update norm exceeds this many times the median are left out of the round; none if unset |
| `size_scaling` | 'none' \| 'sqrt_examples' | `'sqrt_examples'` | none: norms compared as they are; sqrt_examples: each norm divided by the square root of the client's number of examples over the median one, so that a large share is not taken for an outlier (the clipping norm and the logged norms are those of a client of median size) |
| `log_directions` | bool | `False` | logs each client's cosine similarity to the coordinate-wise median update and to its closest other client (clip_cos_median_<cid>, clip_cos_closest_<cid>); costs a copy of every update |

### `fltrust` — FLTrust (trusted examples)

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategydecorator/fltrust`*

FLTrust: clients weighed by the direction of their update against the server's on trusted examples.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server_steps` | 'clients' \| 'epochs' | `'clients'` | clients: the server trains as many optimizer steps as the median client (as the paper's same number of local iterations; set the trusted batch size to the clients'); epochs: local_epochs over the trusted examples |
| `normalize_to` | 'median' \| 'server' | `'median'` | median: every update scaled to the median client update norm; server: to the server update's norm (the paper's), whose few trusted examples may make a step much longer or shorter than the clients' |
| `local_epochs` | int (optional) | `None` | epochs over the trusted examples (server_steps: epochs), or the clients' epochs the steps are counted on; the clients' local epochs if unset |

### `foolsgold` — FoolsGold (alike clients)

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategydecorator/foolsgold`*

FoolsGold: clients weighed down when their history of updates looks like another client's.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kappa` | float | `1.0` | confidence of the logit: larger, the weights go faster to 0 or 1 (the paper's 1) |

### `evaluateonly` — EvaluateOnly

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/strategydecorator/evaluateonly`*

No client trains: each round only evaluates the server's model, on the server's test data and on each client's validation or test data (section), and writes the per-site report: the server, each site and the sites' mean weighted by their examples. Federated evaluation, with the onnxmodel model or the server's weights_path. With server_run.schedule (a deployed model followed every night) or stop_without_new_data, a round counts when a site evaluated: a site without new data does not.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report_name` | str | `'evaluation'` | the per-site report, <name>.json and <name>.csv in the reporting directory, written at each round |
| `section` | 'val' \| 'test' | `'val'` | the section of its data each site evaluates on |

Used by: [`configs/onnx_eval/server.yml`](../configs/onnx_eval/server.yml)

### `upperlevellink` — Upper level link

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins-hierarchical/strategydecorator/upperlevellink`*

Hierarchical sessions: on the server of a lower level, waits for the upper level's model at each round, puts it in place of the session's, and publishes the round's aggregate for the upper level's relay; added last to the pipeline by `server_strategy.upper_level_link`, set by the session managers; see hierarchical-session.md.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `transport` | 'directory' \| 'manager' | `'directory'` | directory: files in a directory shared by the relay and the lower level's server, on one machine; manager: the mailbox of the upper level's session manager, over HTTP, the two ends on any machines |
| `directory` | str | `'/tmp/pybiscus-links'` | transport directory: directory shared by the relay and the lower level's server, on the machine where both run |
| `manager_url` | str | `''` | transport manager: this end's own session manager (the relay's: the upper level's; the lower server's: its level's, which relays to the upper one) |
| `link_id` | str | `'link'` | the same on both ends; a new one for each hierarchical run, files of an earlier run being taken otherwise |
| `timeout` | float | `3600` | seconds to wait for the other level: a whole round of the lower level, or between two rounds of the upper level |
| `poll_interval` | float | `0.5` | transport directory: seconds between two looks at the directory |

## Result modifiers

A change made to a client's result before aggregation (the `result_modifier` of `personalizeclientsfitin`).

### `resultidentity` — ResultIdentity

*core, `pybiscus/flower/resultmodifier/basic`*

Leaves the weights unchanged.

No configuration (`config: {empty_configuration: true}`).

### `result * factor` — ResultMultiply

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/resultmodifier/resultmultiplier`*

Multiplies every weight by `factor`: a simple modification, to try personalizeclientsfitin.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `factor` | float | `1.0` | every weight sent to the client is multiplied by it |

### `client watermarking` — ClientWatermarking

*plugin, `pybiscus-plugins/resultmodifier/clientwatermarking`*

Embeds a fingerprint of each client in the global weights it is sent (the model's `fc` layer carries the watermark), and traces how well each fingerprint can be read back. The match between Flower clients and fingerprints is written to `client_fingerprints_path`, the secret key and each fingerprint to the checkpoints, so that `traitor_tracing` finds which client a leaked model came from. A Flower client that reconnects gets a new cid, hence a new fingerprint.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tag` | str (optional) | `None` | subdirectory of this instance's files; needed when the plugin appears more than once, to save before and after a transformation for instance |
| `nb_clients` | int | `5` | clients to give a fingerprint |
| `key_size_layer` | int | `2112` | weights of the layer that carries the watermark |
| `key_size_fingerprint` | int | `256` | bits of each client's fingerprint |
| `save_as_cp` | bool | `True` | save each watermarked model as a checkpoint |
| `reporting_sub_dir` | str | `'rounds'` | subdirectory of the reporting directory, one round_<n> directory per round inside |
| `client_watermaked_model_prefix` | str | `'client_watermarked_model'` | prefix of the watermarked models' files |
| `client_watermaking_traces_path` | str | `'client_watermarking_traces.txt'` | file of the watermarking traces (WSR of every client) |
| `client_fingerprints_path` | str | `'client_fingerprints.csv'` | file matching each Flower client (cid) with its fingerprint, to find which client a leaked model came from |

Used by: [`configs/watermarking_5_clients/config_server1.yml`](../configs/watermarking_5_clients/config_server1.yml)

## Stopping criteria

When the server ends the session before its `num_rounds`, tested after each round (`server_run.stopping`).

### `threshold` — Metric threshold

*core, `pybiscus/flower/stoppingcriterion/basic`*

Ends the session once a metric reaches a value (an accuracy of 0.98, a loss of 0.05).

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metric` | str | `'accuracy'` | name of the metric, as the strategy reports it (accuracy, loss, f1score…) |
| `source` | 'test' \| 'evaluate' \| 'fit' | `'test'` | which evaluation the metric comes from |
| `goal` | 'maximize' \| 'minimize' | `'maximize'` | maximize: stop once the metric reaches the value or more; minimize: the value or less |
| `value` | float | required | the value to reach |

### `patience` — Metric patience

*core, `pybiscus/flower/stoppingcriterion/basic`*

Ends the session when a metric has not improved for a number of rounds (early stopping).

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `metric` | str | `'loss'` | name of the metric, as the strategy reports it (accuracy, loss, f1score…) |
| `source` | 'test' \| 'evaluate' \| 'fit' | `'test'` | which evaluation the metric comes from |
| `goal` | 'maximize' \| 'minimize' | `'minimize'` | whether the metric improves by going up or down |
| `patience` | int | `3` | rounds without improvement before the session ends |
| `min_delta` | float | `0.0` | a change of the best value smaller than this is no improvement |

### `maxduration` — Maximal duration

*core, `pybiscus/flower/stoppingcriterion/basic`*

Ends the session after a duration: the round under way when it is over is finished.

| field (under `config`) | type | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | float | required | duration of the rounds after which the session ends, from the start of the first one; tested at the end of each round, which is finished |

## Fit results aggregators

How the clients' fit metrics are combined (the `aggregator` of `fedavgwithaggregator`).

### `average` — Average

*core, `pybiscus/flower/flowerfitresultsaggregator/flowerfitresultsaggregatorusingaverage`*

The new weights are the plain average of the clients' weights, whatever their number of examples.

No configuration (`config: {empty_configuration: true}`).

### `weightedaverage` — WeightedAverage

*core, `pybiscus/flower/flowerfitresultsaggregator/flowerfitresultsaggregatorusingweightedaverage`*

The new weights are the average of the clients' weights, each weighted by its number of examples (as FedAvg).

No configuration (`config: {empty_configuration: true}`).
